input.text: The theory of plate tectonics explains the large-scale motion of seven large plates and many smaller plates of Earth's lithosphere. These plates move at rates of 2 to 15 centimetres per year. When plates converge, one may be forced beneath the other in a process called subduction, which can produce earthquakes and volcanic activity along the boundary.
